subtitle: A Gond king holds his fragile realm with stone, song and careful words

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Ramnagar palace against a dusky sky
panels.action: Hridayshah of Garha-Mandla stands on the terrace of Ramnagar Palace, cloaked in royal robes, a veena resting beside his hand, as the Narmada glimmers below and dense forests stretch into the horizon.

dialogue.text: In a Gond kingdom bruised by empire, Hridayshah of Mandla chose a strange armor—palaces, pedigrees and Sanskrit songs—to keep his world from vanishing.

i18n.hi: साम्राज्य से दबे गोंड राज्य में, मandla के हृदयशाह ने अजीब कवच चुना – महल, वंशावली और संस्कृत गीत – ताकि उसकी दुनिया मिट न जाए

panels.shot: bird's-eye view of central India, slowly pushing in toward Mandla
panels.action: A map-like vista of seventeenth-century central India: Mughal banners in the north, Bundela forts to the west, and deep green forests around a modest citadel marked as Mandla, where Hridayshah stands in miniature over his land.

dialogue.text: By the mid-1600s, Garha-Mandla lay in the long shadow of the Mughals and the restless Bundelas. Once mighty Gond lands were now a narrowed strip along the Narmada.

i18n.hi: १६०० के बीच तक गरहा-मandla, मुगलों और बेचैन बुंदेलों की लम्बी परछाई में आ गया था; कभी विशाल गोंड भूभाग अब केवल नर्मदा किनारे की पतली पट्टी रह गया था

panels.shot: medium interior shot of a dim audience hall, focus on young Hridayshah
panels.action: Inside a simple wooden hall, a younger Hridayshah listens sharply as older Gond nobles gesture over a rough map, candles throwing long shadows that hint at past battles and lost territories.

dialogue.text: Hridayshah inherited not the sweeping Garha-Katanga of legend, but its remnant—Garha-Mandla—scarred by earlier Mughal campaigns and internal strain.

i18n.hi: हृदयशाह को किवदंती वाला विशाल गरहा-कटंगा नहीं, उसका बचा-खुचा हिस्सा मिला – गरहा-मandla – जिसे पहले के मुग़ल हमलों और भीतरू तनाव ने घायल किया था

panels.shot: slow push-in on Hridayshah's thoughtful face, half-lit by lamp
panels.action: Close on Hridayshah’s face as he studies a worn family genealogy scroll, his fingers tracing old names while distant drums hint at unrest beyond the palace.

dialogue.text: In these narrow limits, he faced a hard question: how does a Gond king hold his house together when spears alone cannot widen the borders again?

i18n.hi: इन सिकुड़े हदों में उसका कड़ा सवाल था: जब भाले सीमा नहीं बढ़ा सकते, तब गोंड राजा अपना घर कैसे जोड़े रखे?

panels.shot: wide shot of the Narmada bend with construction activity along the bank
panels.action: Along the curving Narmada, workers haul stone and timber as the first walls of Ramnagar’s palace rise; Hridayshah stands on a rocky outcrop overseeing the site, the river mist curling around him.

dialogue.text: One answer was stone. Hridayshah shifted his centre to Ramnagar near Mandla and raised new palaces on the river, binding his line to a fresh seat of power.

i18n.hi: एक जवाब था पत्थर। हृदयशाह ने राजधानी मandla के पास रामनगर लाई और नदी किनारे नए महल उठाए, अपने वंश को नई गद्दी से बाँध दिया

panels.shot: architectural wide shot of an early Moti Mahal courtyard under construction
panels.action: In an unfinished courtyard, arches and pillars of what will become Moti Mahal rise amid scaffolding; craftsmen carve motifs while Hridayshah walks with an architect, gesturing toward the emerging facade.

dialogue.text: Later memory would call one of these halls Moti Mahal. Today scholars still pick through its quiet arches, seeking traces of Gond art under later layers.

i18n.hi: बाद की याद उन्हें मोती महल कहेगी; आज विद्वान उसकी खामोश मेहराबों में खोजते हैं कि बाद की तहों के नीचे गोंड कला के क्या निशान बचे हैं

panels.shot: medium shot on a stone inscription being chiseled, Hridayshah in background
panels.action: A Brahmin scholar, Jaya Govinda, supervises a stonecutter chiselling neat Nagari letters into a slab, while Hridayshah watches from the steps of the palace courtyard.

dialogue.text: Under Hridayshah, the court poet Jaya Govinda set down a dynastic genealogy at Ramnagar, carving the king’s place into stone and memory.

i18n.hi: हृदयशाह के दरबार में कवि जया गोविंद ने रामनगर में वंशावली गढ़ी, राजा का नाम पत्थर और स्मृति दोनों में नक़्श कर दिया

panels.shot: close-up on the inscription surface, camera angled to show Hridayshah's name
panels.action: The chisel pauses as the carved letters of Hridayshah’s name catch the light, while his blurred figure in the background turns toward a distant messenger entering the court.

dialogue.text: That inscription, still read at Mandla, is one of the clearest voices of Garha-Mandla’s own self-story in his age.

i18n.hi: वही शिलालेख, जो आज भी मandla में पढ़ा जाता है, उसके दौर में गरहा-मandla की अपनी आत्मकथा की सबसे साफ़ आवाज़ों में है

panels.shot: interior wide of a modest but refined durbar, Mughal envoy present
panels.action: In a durbar hall adorned with local motifs, Hridayshah sits on a low throne receiving a richly dressed Mughal envoy, both men framed by cautious courtiers and maps of neighboring Bundela lands.

dialogue.text: Beyond stone, there was diplomacy. Hridayshah maintained relations with the Mughal court, threading a path between submission and survival.

i18n.hi: पत्थर से परे, राजनय था। हृदयशाह ने मुग़ल दरबार से नाते रखे, आत्मसमर्पण और बचाव के बीच महीन राह बुनी

panels.shot: medium two-shot of Hridayshah and the envoy in quiet conversation
panels.action: Hridayshah leans forward in measured conversation with the envoy, a scroll bearing imperial seals between them, while outside the hall, armed guards watch the forested horizon.

dialogue.speaker: hridayshah
dialogue.text: Let the Narmada mark our peace. A small kingdom can still stand firm.

i18n.hi: नर्मदा हमारी सुलह की रेखा रहे। छोटा राज भी डट कर खड़ा रह सकता है

panels.shot: wide shot of Bundela horsemen on a ridge, Mandla in distant background
panels.action: Armoured Bundela riders survey the distant silhouette of Mandla’s fort from a rocky ridge, the dry wind whipping their banners as the dense forest lies between them and the Gond capital.

dialogue.text: To the west, Bundela powers probed and pressed. Garha-Mandla could not ignore them, yet could not match them field for field.

i18n.hi: पश्चिम से बुंदेला ताकतें टटोलती, धकेलती रहीं; गरहा-मandla उन्हें अनदेखा नहीं कर सकता था, पर मैदान में बराबरी भी नहीं कर सकता था

panels.shot: medium shot of Hridayshah between a war council and a music chamber door
panels.action: In a palace corridor, Hridayshah stands at a junction: to one side an open door to a war council with armour laid out, to the other a dim chamber from which the faint outline of a veena and manuscripts can be seen.

dialogue.text: The choice was not war or peace alone. Hridayshah’s answer drew also from quieter rooms—the chambers of music and text.

i18n.hi: चुनाव सिर्फ़ जंग या सुलह नहीं था। हृदयशाह का जवाब और भी शांत कोठरियों से निकला – संगीत और ग्रंथों के कक्षों से

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of Hridayshah seated with a veena and palm-leaf manuscripts
panels.action: Hridayshah sits cross-legged on a woven mat, a veena resting across his lap, palm-leaf manuscripts beside him as he listens to a court musician, the lamplight softening the stone walls.

dialogue.text: Later tradition would remember him not only as king, but as a musician-king, linked to Sanskrit treatises named Hriday Koutuk and Hriday Prakash.

i18n.hi: बाद की परंपरा उसे सिर्फ़ राजा नहीं, बल्कि संगीतज्ञ-राजा कहती है, जिसे हृदय कौतुक और हृदय प्रकाश जैसे संस्कृत ग्रंथों से जोड़ा गया

panels.shot: close-up on Hridayshah's hand turning a palm leaf, text hinted but unreadable
panels.action: His hand gently turns a palm leaf inscribed with fine Sanskrit script, the exact words indistinct, while a faint outline of musical notation marks the leaf’s margin.

dialogue.text: These works, dated around 1660 in later music histories, are rare signs of a Gond ruler tied to Sanskrit musicology—even if critical editions remain scarce today.

i18n.hi: संगीत इतिहास में लगभग १६६० के आस-पास दिनांकित ये रचनाएँ, संस्कृत संगीत-शास्त्र से जुड़े किसी गोंड नरेश के विरले चिन्ह हैं – भले ही ठोस आलोच्य संस्करण आज भी कम मिलते हों

panels.shot: medium shot of Hridayshah guiding a scribe in a quiet study
panels.action: In a small study lined with niches, Hridayshah gestures as a Brahmin scribe writes on palm leaves, while a musician nearby plucks a string to test a note.

dialogue.text: Scholars debate the exact contents, but their attributed authorship marks a bridge: Gond court, Sanskrit learning, and musical thought touching each other in Mandla.

i18n.hi: विद्वान इनके असली रूप पर बहस करते हैं, पर उनका नामी लेखन एक पुल दिखाता है: गोंड दरबार, संस्कृत विद्या और संगीत-चिंतन, जो मandla में एक-दूसरे को छूते हैं

panels.shot: wide shot of a moonlit palace courtyard where soldiers and musicians share space
panels.action: Under a clear moon, soldiers drill in one corner of the Ramnagar courtyard while, in another, musicians rehearse before Hridayshah, who sits between them, listening with a grave, intent gaze.

dialogue.text: In this fragile Gond state, spears and songs were not rivals. Culture became a second defense, shaping loyalty, identity and the court’s image to the wider world.

i18n.hi: इस नाज़ुक गोंड राज्य में भाले और गीत दुश्मन नहीं थे; संस्कृति दूसरी ढाल बनी, जिसने निष्ठा, पहचान और दरबार की छवि को दूर-दराज़ तक गढ़ा

panels.shot: documentary-style shot of a colonial-era visitor sketching Ramnagar ruins
panels.action: Centuries later, a British-era visitor in simple travel clothes sketches the aging facades of Ramnagar’s palace, its plaster peeling, while local guides point out old halls said to be Hridayshah’s.

dialogue.text: Eyre Chatterton, writing in 1916, gathered stories of Hridayshah, including a tale of ‘sixteen tigers’—a legend historians flag as late and uncertain.

i18n.hi: १९१६ में लिखते हुए आयर चैटरटॉन ने हृदयशाह की कहानियाँ जुटाईं, जिनमें ‘सोलह बाघों’ की कथा भी थी – जिसे इतिहासकार देर से बनी, संदिग्ध दंतकथा मानते हैं

panels.shot: slow push-in on present-day Ramnagar palace facade, half-ruined yet imposing
panels.action: The camera lingers on the weathered yet imposing facade of Ramnagar’s palace today, plants creeping through cracks, as invisible visitors walk through, imagining the Gond court that once stood here.

dialogue.text: Modern heritage work now returns to these halls, reading stone, inscription and rumor to recover a Gond king whose tools were not only swords.

i18n.hi: आज की विरासत टीमें फिर इन दीवारों में लौटती हैं, पत्थर, लेख और अफ़वाह पढ़कर उस गोंड राजा को वापस खोजती हैं, जिसके हथियार सिर्फ़ तलवारें नहीं थे

panels.shot: final contemplative shot of Hridayshah on a terrace, blending into present ruins
panels.action: Hridayshah stands again on the Ramnagar terrace at sunset, veena beside him; as the scene fades, his figure dissolves into the present-day ruins viewed from the same angle.

dialogue.text: Hridayshah’s borders did not grow, yet his palaces, inscriptions and faint music-books show another kind of rule—where a small kingdom tries to outlast conquest through memory and song.

i18n.hi: हृदयशाह की सीमाएँ नहीं बढ़ीं, पर उसके महल, शिलालेख और धुंधले संगीत-ग्रंथ एक और तरह की हुकूमत दिखाते हैं – जहाँ छोटा राज्य याद और गीत के सहारे फ़तह पर भारी पड़ने की कोशिश करता है

subtitle_i18n.en: A Gond king holds his fragile realm with stone, song and careful words
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक गोंड राजा पत्थर, गीत और नपी-तुली बातों से अपनी नाज़ुक रियासत थामे है
